output.summary: KEP-4460 proposes replacing the kube-apiserver's timeout filter with per-request read/write deadlines via the Go ResponseController, behind the alpha feature gate PerHandlerReadWriteTimeout, so the whole handler runs on one goroutine. Status is implementable at alpha.
output.rationale: The timeout filter has caused many hard-to-debug data races, and it runs the inner handler in a separate goroutine that cannot be killed externally. Removing it and setting request-scoped read/write deadlines equal to the request context deadline keeps timeout behavior close to today for short, non-long-running requests. The reviewers raised concerns about client behavior changes (HTTP/1 connection close, HTTP/2 stream resets) and about how the handler goroutine would be stopped, and the design treats these as open questions to address during alpha.

alternatives.why_not: The author states 'we are not going to use net/http.TimeoutHandler', and enj notes it is strictly worse than the existing handler.

alternatives.option: Set a short server-wide timeout and extend it for long-running requests
alternatives.why_not: tkashem replied that long-running requests are outside the scope of this proposal, since no deadline is set on their request context today.

alternatives.option: Spin up a monitoring goroutine only for requests that time out, or track all in-flight requests globally
alternatives.why_not: Wojtek suggested avoiding global tracking of inflight requests; tkashem said the goroutine-only approach needs a way to be notified when the context expires, and proposed global tracking as an alpha option with a beta criterion to replace it. The sources do not say which was finally chosen.

alternatives.option: Panic from the ResponseWriter Write method or from context Value after timeout
alternatives.why_not: The thread notes the context package can call Value from other goroutines, so a panic there could kill the process; the approach is still under investigation, and panic-on-write is described as an option, not a settled decision.

evidence.quote: the `timeout` filter in the kube-apiserver will become redundant, and thus be removed from the server handler chain.
A new feature flag `PerHandlerReadWriteTimeout` will be introduced, when enabled:
The scope of this proposal is the same, short (non long-running) requests only.
With a featuregate, I think we can try removing our special cased timeout handler.
it merged before my PRR review, but this looks fine for Alpha.
